_about: Observations from the figures (looked at the images; marked as observations in the document). Keys = cluster ids of q002_all_fits_summary_docx.py (mv:/ov:/sr:/fs:<section>/<rel with <STEM>>). Written 2026-11-19/20 from contact sheets of the inputs; full-set entries are added after the new-law full sets exist and have been viewed. A cluster without an entry gets no observation paragraph. Full-set entries written 2026-11-20 (CST) after viewing the contact sheets of the ten new-law full sets (tests/q002_all_fits_20261120/sheets_q002/).
ov:best: Above the late window the curves of the six runs lie close together at this scale. In the late window D2's model NG stays below the data and below the other runs at the end, A and D put the model RG above the RG data near touchdown, and C f10/1e-4 follows the NG data most closely.
ov:C: Above the late window the six curves lie close together at this scale; the differences are in the late window, where the two P_m 1e-4 chains nearly coincide and C f10/0.01 off departs most from the RG data near touchdown while its NG stays below the NG data at the end.
mv:vo: In every run the new-law (solid) and old-law (dashed) curves lie close together above the late window at this scale; the visible differences are in the late window. The two P_m 1e-4 chains show nearly coinciding curves; in C f10/0.01 off the new-law RG falls well below the RG data in the last metres; in D2 the new-law NG stays below the data and below the old-law curve at the end.
mv:residuals: D2's new-law NG residual falls to the most negative value at the end of the descent, while in the other five runs shown the NG residual rises to positive values at the last points with both laws; above the late window the new- and old-law residuals nearly coincide in every run shown.
mv:convergence: The two option-C chains with P_m 0.01 and templates on drop within the first cycle and then stay flat; C f10/0.01 off stays flat from the first fit; in A the new-law curve lies below the old-law one in every cycle; in the other chains it lies above.
sr:inspection: Within each run the new-law (a, b) and old-law (c, d) maps show a similar spatial pattern of the seen production at this scale; panels (e, f) look the same in all runs (same time and geometry).

fs:source_areas/12M_source_area_union_NG: D2: narrow elongated features along steep terrain and a cluster east of the impact area; softplus: one compact elliptical region south-east of the impact point; A and D: extended areas of many degrees in longitude and latitude around the impact point (A also north-east of the impact region in the global map); B: a compact core just east of the impact point with scattered facets of the larger P over a wider area; C with P_m 1e-4: only small thin features, hardly visible at this scale; C with P_m 0.01 (f1, f10): a compact patch south-east of the impact point and small features near it; C f10/0.01 off: an area north-west of the impact point and features next to it. The close-up boxes differ between runs, so equal sizes on the page are not equal areas.
